## Baileys (@whiskeysockets/baileys) — Findings, July 2026

**What it is**
- WebSockets-based TypeScript/Node library for the WhatsApp Web multi-device protocol; interfaces directly via WebSocket, does **not** require Selenium, a browser, or Puppeteer. [github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys), [npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys)
- Project migrated from the original `@adiwajshing/baileys` to the `@WhiskeySockets` org (now the canonical maintained fork). [github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys)

**Linking methods**
- Two methods: (1) **QR code** printed to terminal, scanned from the phone's WhatsApp; (2) **Pairing code** — an 8-digit code generated by phone number, entered in WhatsApp (Link a Device → Link with phone number instead), no QR needed. [npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys)
- Baileys authenticates as a **companion/linked device** (a "second WhatsApp client") under WhatsApp's multi-device API — up to 4 companion devices + 1 main phone per account. [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys), [engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device/)

**⚠️ CRITICAL PRIVACY FINDING — linked devices share the account and chats (YES)**
- A linked/companion device shares the **same WhatsApp account and message history** as the primary phone. On linking, the primary device transfers an encrypted bundle of recent chats to the new device; WhatsApp then **synchronizes message history and app state (contacts, archive/star status, new incoming and outgoing messages) across all devices**, end-to-end encrypted between them. [engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device/)
- **So if Baileys is linked to someone's personal number, every message the bot sends or receives WOULD appear in that person's WhatsApp app on their primary phone** — it is the same account, same chat threads. There is no isolation between the bot's traffic and the owner's normal WhatsApp. Each time the companion connects it displays all the latest messages. [engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device/)
- The owner can also **see the linked device in Settings → Linked Devices** (with last-used time) and can remotely log it out. So the link is visible, not hidden. [engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/07/14/security/whatsapp-multi-device/)
- **Isolation conclusion:** to keep bot traffic separate from a person's personal chats, you must link Baileys to a **separate, dedicated WhatsApp number** — not the owner's personal number.

**Personal vs dedicated number**
- Real-project guidance is explicit: **never use your primary/personal or business-critical number.** Use a dedicated bot number, keep backups of session state, and don't rely on it for revenue-critical messaging. [wasenderapi.com/blog/how-to-use-evolution-api-without-getting-banned-on-whatsapp-2026-guide](https://wasenderapi.com/blog/how-to-use-evolution-api-without-getting-banned-on-whatsapp-2026-guide), [lumadock.com/tutorials/hermes-whatsapp-baileys-gateway](https://lumadock.com/tutorials/hermes-whatsapp-baileys-gateway)

**ToS / ban risk**
- Baileys is **unofficial** — "not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with WhatsApp." The repo warns against ToS violations and against stalkerware/bulk/automated-messaging use. [github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys)
- Using it against a normal account violates WhatsApp ToS (which prohibit unofficial/modified clients and non-personal/bulk/automated messaging on the consumer app); the number **can be banned at any time**, and bans on unofficial-API accounts are generally **permanent with no effective appeal**. [whatsapp.checkleaked.cc/blog/whatsapp-cloud-api-vs-unofficial](https://whatsapp.checkleaked.cc/blog/whatsapp-cloud-api-vs-unofficial), [wasenderapi.com](https://wasenderapi.com/blog/how-to-use-evolution-api-without-getting-banned-on-whatsapp-2026-guide)
- One 2026 SMB analysis: ~68% of surveyed businesses using unofficial WhatsApp automation reported at least one ban within 12 months; reverse-engineered-Web tools (Baileys, WAHA, Evolution API) often "last 2–8 weeks before detection." (Third-party blog stat, treat as indicative not authoritative.) [blog.kraya-ai.com/whatsapp-automation-ban-risk](https://blog.kraya-ai.com/whatsapp-automation-ban-risk)

**Maintenance status (2026) — actively maintained**
- Latest release **v7.0.0-rc13, published May 21, 2026** (~2 months ago); ~46 total releases; v7.0.0 introduced breaking changes with a migration guide at whiskey.so/migrate-latest. [github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/releases](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/releases), [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@whiskeysockets/baileys)

**GitHub stars**
- Roughly **10.2k stars**. [github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys)

# Running an AI Agent on WhatsApp — Technical Research (July 2026)

Build-brief input for NanoClaw (Node/TS agent platform, Telegram working, adding WhatsApp).
Hard constraint driving the recommendation: **the owner must NOT see the agent's chats inside his own personal WhatsApp app.**

---

## 0) The one finding that decides everything

WhatsApp has two fundamentally different worlds:

1. **Linked-device libraries (Baileys, whatsapp-web.js, Whapi.cloud)** attach as a *companion device* to an existing WhatsApp account. A companion device **shares the same account and the same message history** as the primary phone. WhatsApp synchronizes incoming + outgoing messages, contacts, archive/star state across all devices, E2E-encrypted between them (Meta's own multi-device design). → **If you link the agent to the owner's personal number, every message the agent sends/receives appears in the owner's WhatsApp app, and the linked device is visible in Settings → Linked Devices.** There is no isolation. (engineering.fb.com multi-device writeup.)

2. **Official Cloud API (Meta) / BSPs on top of it** turn a phone number into an *API-only business number*. That number **can no longer be used in the normal WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app** — the account is API-controlled, chats live only where your server puts them. The owner has no app view of it at all. Confirmed one-way door: to register a number already on consumer WhatsApp you must delete that account first (wipes history), and reversing requires deregistering from Cloud API.

**Therefore, given "owner must not see the chats," the isolation is achieved by number choice, not by software choice:**
- Either a **dedicated number the agent owns** (any approach), or
- The **official Cloud API** (which is dedicated-by-construction).

Linking any tool to the owner's *personal* number fails the constraint outright.

---

## 1) Connection approaches — comparison

| Approach | Official? | Owner's *personal* # usable while keeping chats hidden? | Pairing | ToS / ban risk | Rough cost | Prod-ready | Pilot today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WhatsApp Business Cloud API** (Meta direct) | ✅ Yes | N/A — number becomes API-only, removed from the app (isolation by construction) | Meta embedded signup + number registration (6-digit PIN) | None (sanctioned) | Per-message (see below); infra only | ✅ High | ⚠️ Hours–days (verification, template approval) |
| **Baileys** `@whiskeysockets/baileys` | ❌ No | Only on a **dedicated** number; on the personal number chats WOULD show | QR **or** 8-digit pairing code | High — unofficial, permanent ban risk | Free (self-host) | ⚠️ Grey-area | ✅ Minutes |
| **whatsapp-web.js** | ❌ No | Same as Baileys — dedicated number only | QR (pairing code also supported) | High — same as Baileys | Free (self-host, +Chromium RAM) | ⚠️ Grey-area | ✅ Minutes |
| **Twilio WhatsApp** | ✅ Yes (Cloud API reseller) | Dedicated business sender | Sandbox keyword / Meta verify | None | $0.005/msg + Meta fee | ✅ High | ✅ Sandbox in minutes |
| **360dialog** | ✅ Yes (BSP, direct Cloud API) | Dedicated business number | Meta BSP onboarding | None | €49–249/mo flat + Meta **at cost, no markup** | ✅ High | ⚠️ Days (verify) |
| **WATI** | ✅ Yes (SaaS on API) | Dedicated business number | SaaS + Meta verify | None | $59–279/mo + ~20% msg markup | ✅ High (no-code) | ⚠️ Fast after verify |
| **Whapi.cloud** | ❌ No (hosted unofficial, wraps WA-Web like Baileys) | Yes, uses a regular # via QR — but that means **the linked account's app sees the chats** unless it's a dedicated number | QR / pairing code | High — unofficial | $29/mo per number flat, free sandbox | ⚠️ Grey-area | ✅ Minutes |

### 1a) WhatsApp Business Cloud API (official)
- **Setup:** Meta developer app → "Connect with customers through WhatsApp" use case → link a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA). Test number + temp token for dev; production needs a system user + permanent token (`whatsapp_business_messaging`, `whatsapp_business_management`, `business_management`). **Embedded Signup** is Meta's OAuth onboarding that registers the number and auto-subscribes webhooks — the right primitive if NanoClaw onboards many owners.
- **Webhook model:** inbound = HTTPS POST to your public endpoint; GET handshake echoes `hub.challenge` + verify token; subscribe to the `messages` field. Outbound = Graph API POST to the phone-number-ID messages endpoint.
- **Personal number:** to register a number already on consumer WhatsApp you must delete that account first (wipes history); once on Cloud API it **cannot be used in the normal WhatsApp/Business app**. Reversible only by deregistering. (A special BSP "coexistence"/Multi-solution mode is the only exception, and it's not standard registration.)
- **24-hour window:** customer messages first → 24h free-form reply window, reset by each new inbound. Click-to-WhatsApp ads / Page CTA open a **72h** free window.
- **Templates:** any business-initiated message outside the window must be a **pre-approved template** (Marketing / Utility / Authentication).

### 1b) 2026 pricing (important change)
- **Per-conversation pricing is deprecated.** Meta moved to **per-message pricing effective July 1, 2025**; every delivered template billed individually by category + recipient country.
- Representative US rates 2026: **Marketing ≈ $0.025/msg, Utility ≈ $0.004, Authentication ≈ $0.004, Service (free-form in-window) = free.** Utility templates inside an open service window are free; Auth is not.
- Rates follow the **recipient's** country. Examples (Marketing): India ≈ $0.0094, Brazil ≈ $0.0625, UK ≈ $0.048, UAE ≈ $0.0499, Germany > $0.124.
- The old **"1,000 free service conversations/month" allowance was removed** — replaced by *all* in-window service messages being free, uncapped.

### 1c) Baileys
- TypeScript/Node **WebSocket** client of the WA multi-device protocol — **no browser/Puppeteer**, ~50 MB RAM, sub-second start. Scales to many numbers per box cheaply.
- Links as a companion device via **QR or 8-digit pairing code**. Up to 4 companion devices + 1 phone.
- **Unofficial**, violates WhatsApp ToS; numbers can be **permanently banned** with no real appeal.
- **Maintained:** migrated `@adiwajshing` → `@WhiskeySockets`; latest **v7.0.0-rc13, May 21 2026**; **~10k stars**.

### 1d) whatsapp-web.js
- **Puppeteer-based** — drives a headless Chromium WhatsApp Web session. "Batteries-included," simpler API, but **~0.5 GB RAM per session** (Chromium). **~22k stars**, **v1.34.7 Apr 24 2026**, actively maintained.
- QR primary; **pairing code supported** (`pairWithPhoneNumber` + `'code'` event; can hit 429 rate limits).
- Same linked-device model, same ToS/ban risk. **Full group support.**
- vs Baileys: pick Baileys for lightweight/many-number/browser-free; whatsapp-web.js for a simple all-in-one API when Chromium overhead is fine.

### 1e) BSPs / wrappers
- **Twilio:** official Cloud API reseller. **Sandbox = live in minutes** (join a shared test number by keyword, $15 trial credit) — best instant test. $0.005/msg on top of Meta's per-template fee. Prod = Business Manager verification + template approval (days).
- **360dialog:** official BSP, **direct Cloud API, no markup** — flat €49/€99/€249 per month per number, Meta fees passed through at cost. Cheapest at scale; you build your own UI.
- **WATI:** no-code SaaS (inbox + broadcast + chatbot builder), $59–279/mo **+ ~20% markup** on Meta rates. For non-technical SMB teams.
- **Whapi.cloud:** **unofficial hosted** wrapper of the WA-Web session (Baileys-class mechanism, but managed). Uses a regular number via QR, **full groups/channels/status**, **$29/mo per number flat**, sandbox free. Fastest unofficial path, same ban risk, and same privacy caveat: whatever number you link, that account's app sees the chats.

---

## 2) Privacy / isolation — the precise answers

- **Do Baileys / whatsapp-web.js chats appear in the linked number's WhatsApp app?** **YES.** They connect as companion devices; WhatsApp syncs all incoming/outgoing messages and app state across every device of the account. Linked to the owner's personal number → the owner sees every agent chat, and sees the linked device listed. **This violates the constraint.**
- **Clean isolation pattern real projects use:** link the unofficial library to a **separate, dedicated number the agent owns** — never the owner's primary/personal number. Universally recommended ("never use your primary/business-critical number") both for privacy and because bans kill the number.
- **Why dedicated is standard:** (1) companion devices can't be partitioned — one account = one shared history; (2) ban risk on unofficial APIs means you never want it hitting a number that matters; a throwaway dedicated line contains the blast radius.
- **Getting a dedicated number that WhatsApp will actually verify (2026):**
  - WhatsApp runs carrier-type lookups and **rejects VoIP ranges.** **Google Voice — rejected. TextNow — rejected.**
  - **Travel data eSIMs (Airalo etc.) — cannot receive the verification SMS/call** (data-only, no MSISDN). Useless as the verification number.
  - **Twilio** is *not* a way to verify a personal-style number for an unofficial client — Twilio's WhatsApp product **is** the official Business API sender (different world).
  - **What reliably works:** a **real physical prepaid SIM/eSIM from an actual carrier** (90–99% verification success, ownable, persistent) — the recommended isolation line. Paid single-use services that route real mobile numbers and list WhatsApp (**SMS-Activate, 5SIM, SMSPVA**) pass verification but are **rented/temporary** — fine for a throwaway pilot, risky for a long-lived account (re-verification may fail).
- **Cloud API isolation:** confirmed clean **by construction.** The number becomes API-only, **removed from the normal WhatsApp/Business app**, chats exist only server-side. The owner has no app surface for them. This is the strongest answer to "must feel secure / owner never sees them."

---

## 3) Reference GitHub repos (real, star counts checked)

- **WhiskeySockets/Baileys** (~10k, TS) — the core WA-Web socket library; the connection layer most Node/TS bots build on. Actively maintained (v7 RC, 2026). https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys
- **pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js** (~22k, JS) — Puppeteer-based client; full groups; heavier. https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js
- **askrella/whatsapp-chatgpt** (~3.8k, TS) — whatsapp-web.js + GPT + DALL·E + voice. Richest TS reference but ⚠️ frozen/seeking maintainers. https://github.com/askrella/whatsapp-chatgpt
- **danielgross/whatsapp-gpt** (~3.1k, Go+Python) — original viral "whatsapp-gpt"; ⚠️ unmaintained (2023), historical. https://github.com/danielgross/whatsapp-gpt
- **fathonix/ChatGPT-WhatsApp** (Baileys, TS) — ChatGPT bot rewritten onto Baileys to drop Chromium. Closest clean Baileys+LLM starter. https://github.com/fathonix/ChatGPT-WhatsApp
- **wassengerhq/whatsapp-chatgpt-bot** (~170, Node) — managed-API path; GPT-4o + RAG + MCP + function-calling; maintained. https://github.com/wassengerhq/whatsapp-chatgpt-bot
- **mortium91/langchain-assistant** (~160, Python) — Twilio + LangChain across WhatsApp/Telegram; official-API pattern. https://github.com/mortium91/langchain-assistant
- **yesbhautik/Whatsapp-Ai-BOT** (Node) — Baileys + ChatGPT/DALL·E; popular beginner starter. https://github.com/yesbhautik/Whatsapp-Ai-BOT

Pattern: highest-star repos (askrella, danielgross) are unmaintained; recent maintained work has moved to **Baileys v7** and Cloud-API wrappers. For NanoClaw's Node/TS stack, **Baileys is the connection layer to standardize on**; fathonix/yesbhautik are the closest starters; wassenger shows the managed-Cloud-API alternative.

---

## 4) Operational requirements & the two paths

**Unofficial (Baileys / whatsapp-web.js) — what it needs from us:**
- A **dedicated number** (physical prepaid SIM/eSIM recommended) linked once via QR/pairing code.
- Persist session/auth state (so relink isn't needed each restart); back it up.
- **No public HTTPS endpoint, no Meta verification, no templates** — it's an outbound WebSocket/browser session from our host. This mirrors how NanoClaw's Telegram long-poll model already works (self-contained process, no inbound webhook).
- Host: any always-on Node process. Baileys is light (~50 MB); whatsapp-web.js needs Chromium (~0.5 GB/session).

**Official Cloud API — what it needs from us:**
- Meta Business Manager + **Business Verification**; a Meta app; a WABA.
- A **dedicated number** registered to Cloud API (6-digit PIN; **cannot be a number you still want in the WhatsApp app**).
- A **public HTTPS webhook** (GET verify + POST handler, subscribe `messages`) — NanoClaw already has `provision.shellano.com` tunnel infra to expose one.
- Message **templates pre-approved** for anything outside the 24h window.
- Host: the webhook receiver + Graph API sender.

**(A) Fastest pilot today, honoring "owner must not see chats":**
Baileys linked to a **dedicated prepaid SIM/eSIM** (not the owner's number). Minutes to stand up, reuses NanoClaw's no-webhook self-contained pattern, isolation is clean because it's a separate account the owner never opens in an app. Accept the grey-area/ban risk for a pilot; keep session state backed up. (Whapi.cloud $29/mo is the zero-code equivalent if we'd rather not host the socket.)
*If a compliant test is preferred:* Twilio Sandbox is live in minutes but chats route through a Twilio/Meta business sender, not a WhatsApp-app account.

**(B) Right path for production:**
**Official WhatsApp Business Cloud API**, ideally via **360dialog** (direct Cloud API, flat fee, no per-message markup) or Meta-direct. Isolation is guaranteed by construction (API-only number, invisible to any WhatsApp app), no ban risk, sanctioned scaling tiers. The costs are per-message pricing + the 24h-window/template discipline. This is the only path that satisfies both "owner must not see the chats" **and** "must feel secure" without standing on a bannable grey-area client.

---

## 5) Gotchas

- **Messaging window:** free-form replies only inside the 24h customer-service window (72h for ad/CTA entry points); outside → pre-approved template only. (Cloud API/BSP only; unofficial clients have no window concept but carry ban risk instead.)
- **Template pre-approval:** Marketing/Utility/Authentication categories, each billed differently; approval takes time — provision templates before launch.
- **Rate limits / tiers (Cloud API):** messaging limit = unique *new* conversations/24h. New unverified accounts start at **250/day** → 1K → 10K → 100K → unlimited as verification + quality rating improve (1K→10K needs ≥500 unique users in 7 days). Throughput default **80 msg/s**, up to 1,000 msg/s at top tier. Number registration itself is limited to 10 requests / 72h (error 133016).
- **Ban patterns (unofficial):** fresh numbers blasting messages, non-opt-in contacts, bulk sends → soft/hard bans, often permanent. Warm new numbers slowly; message opt-ins only; never link a number that matters. (A vendor blog claims ~68% of unofficial-automation SMBs saw a ban within 12 months and tools last "2–8 weeks" under aggressive use — **directional, not authoritative**; the qualitative pattern is well-supported.)
- **Media:** Cloud API handles media via upload/media-ID + typed messages; unofficial clients (esp. whatsapp-web.js) support rich media but cost RAM/latency.
- **Groups — corrected for 2026:**
  - **Unofficial (Baileys / whatsapp-web.js / Whapi):** full native group support (create, add/remove, admin, send/receive).
  - **Cloud API:** the old "no groups at all" is now **outdated** — Meta shipped a **Groups API** (Official Business Account only, **max 8 participants/group**, up to 10k groups/number, API-managed groups only, no calling/disappearing/interactive msgs). But it **still cannot message arbitrary existing consumer groups** — only groups the API creates/manages. So for real consumer-group participation, unofficial clients remain the only option.
